{"model": "deepseek-flash", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "你在为一款防剧透阅读器更新“前情提要”。读者已读到《jekyll》的「THE LAST NIGHT」结束。
只能使用下面的材料，绝不能写入任何后文情节，即使你知道这部作品。

【此前的前情提要】
During a Sunday walk, Utterson and Enfield stop at a sinister door. Enfield recalls how a man trampled a girl, then paid her family £100 with a cheque that proved genuine. Enfield names him Hyde, deformed and detestable, still holding the key. Utterson says he knows the other party’s name. They agree never to speak of it again.

Utterson returns home troubled and studies Jekyll’s will, which leaves everything to Edward Hyde if Jekyll vanishes. He calls it madness and fears disgrace. At Cavendish Square, Lanyon says Jekyll grew too fanciful years ago and has never heard of Hyde. Unable to sleep, Utterson resolves to hunt Hyde. Keeping watch by the by-street door, he accosts a small man with a key, who admits Jekyll is out, gives his Soho address, then snarls and disappears inside. At Jekyll’s house, Poole confirms Hyde has a key, comes by the dissecting room, and all servants must obey him. Utterson goes home fearing Jekyll is in deep waters.

After dinner, Utterson stays behind with Dr. Jekyll and raises the will. Jekyll calls Lanyon a hide-bound pedant. When Utterson mentions young Hyde, Jekyll pales and refuses to hear more. Utterson offers confidential help, but Jekyll says he can be rid of Hyde whenever he chooses, yet takes great interest in him. Jekyll asks Utterson to help Hyde for his sake when he is gone. Utterson promises to bear with Hyde and get his rights.

【之后各章梗概】
【THE CAREW MURDER CASE】A maid saw Hyde cane Sir Danvers Carew to death and fainted. At two she called police; the mangled body bore a sealed envelope for Utterson, who identified Carew. Inspector Newcomen showed the broken stick, which Utterson recognized as Jekyll’s gift. They searched Hyde’s rooms, finding the other half and a burnt cheque book. Hyde had thousands at the bank, but few familiars, no photograph, and wildly differing descriptions.
【INCIDENT OF THE LETTER】Poole admits Utterson to Jekyll’s cabinet. Utterson asks if Jekyll has heard the news; Jekyll swears he will never see Hyde again. Jekyll gives Utterson a letter signed Edward Hyde, saying he burned the envelope, which had no postmark, and that Hyde dictated his will. Poole says no letter came except by post. Hearing newsboys cry an M.P.’s murder, Utterson shows Guest the murderer’s letter. Guest finds it identical to Jekyll’s note. Utterson locks it in his safe, suspecting forgery.
【INCIDENT OF DR. LANYON】After Sir Danvers Carew’s murder, Hyde vanishes and rewards are offered. Jekyll resumes old friendships, dining with Utterson and Lanyon. Then Jekyll shuts his door; Poole says he is confined. Utterson finds Lanyon decayed, doomed, refusing Jekyll’s name. Jekyll writes of an incurable quarrel and extreme seclusion. Lanyon dies within a fortnight. After the funeral, Utterson opens Lanyon’s sealed envelope, not to be opened till Jekyll’s death or disappearance. Utterson prefers speaking with Poole at the door; Poole reports Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory, silent.
【INCIDENT AT THE WINDOW】On their Sunday walk, Utterson and Enfield stop at the by-street door. Enfield says the Hyde affair is over, but Utterson admits he once saw Hyde and felt the same repulsion. Enfield reveals the door is Dr. Jekyll's back way. Looking up, Utterson sees Jekyll sadly at the middle window. Jekyll says he is very low and it will not last long. He declines their walk, saying he dare not. When Utterson suggests talking from below, Jekyll's smile becomes abject terror and the window is thrust down. The two men leave the court in silence, pale with horror, Utterson saying “God forgive us” twice.
【THE LAST NIGHT】Poole comes to Utterson at night, fearing foul play. They walk to Jekyll’s house, where servants huddle terrified. Poole leads Utterson to the cabinet; a changed voice refuses them. Poole claims Jekyll was murdered eight days ago and saw a masked dwarf—Mr. Hyde. Utterson resolves to break in. Poole strikes the door five times with an axe. Inside lies Hyde’s contorted body, a crushed phial nearby. They search for Jekyll but find only chemicals, a blasphemous book, a will naming Utterson, and a sealed packet. Utterson plans to read the documents and return before midnight.
